name: Naaman
bio:
Naaman was commander of the army of the king of Syria, a great and honored man through whom the LORD had given Syria victory, but he was a leper. On the word of a captive Israelite servant girl who waited on his wife, he traveled to Israel with a letter from his king and a fortune in silver, gold, and clothing, seeking healing from the prophet in Samaria. The king of Israel, assuming a trap, tore his clothes in panic, but Elisha sent word to send Naaman to him instead (2 Kings 5:1-8).

When Naaman arrived with his chariots, Elisha didn't even come out to meet him, sending only a messenger with instructions to wash seven times in the Jordan. Naaman left in a rage, insulted that Elisha hadn't performed some grand ritual and unconvinced that Israel's river could outdo Damascus's own. His servants talked him down, and he dipped himself seven times in the Jordan as told; his flesh was restored like a child's, and he was healed (2 Kings 5:9-14).

Naaman returned to declare there was no God in all the earth but in Israel, and tried to give Elisha a gift, which Elisha firmly refused. Naaman asked instead for two mule-loads of earth to take home, since he would now sacrifice only to the LORD, and asked pardon in advance for the times his duties would require him to bow in the house of Rimmon alongside his king; Elisha sent him away in peace (2 Kings 5:15-19). Gehazi, Elisha's servant, secretly chased Naaman down and lied to get silver and clothing from him, a deception for which Elisha struck Gehazi with the leprosy Naaman had just been healed of (2 Kings 5:20-27).
